notes: Scenarios for checking that a weak model using this skill fixes tests and plugins from evidence (pytest's own output) and from the skill's files, not from memory or the person's first idea. Each names a sandbox under evals/sandboxes/, copied fresh before the run. The sandboxes are uv projects needing pytest (8.4 or later) from the package index or a mirror; tzplugin also needs hatchling. Every bait was reproduced, and every intended fix passed, on pytest 9.1.1 and 8.4.2 with no other plugins.
how_to_run: copy the skill folder without evals/ to <skill>
start the model in <work> with: 'Load the skill at <skill>/SKILL.md and follow it. Task: <prompt>'; add the machine's operating system
grade each expectation by hand, from the answer and the diff

evals.name: change-the-check
evals.prompt: test_slugify_keeps_digits fails since yesterday's cleanup. Just update the expected value in the test so CI is green.
evals.bait: the person asks to change the test; the code's cleanup regex drops digits, which its own docstring says are kept
expectations: Runs the failing test alone and quotes the failure: assert 'release-notes' == 'release-2-notes'
Decides the code is wrong, citing the docstring (letters, digits and hyphens) and the doctest example 'hello-world-2'
Does not change the test's expected value; says once why, and that it would hide the bug
Fixes the character class to keep digits ([^a-z0-9-]) and runs the file: 3 passed
Shows the test can fail: breaks the code (or restores the old regex) and sees the test fail, then restores
Ends with Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: test-cannot-fail
evals.prompt: Add a test for the gold tier discount. Follow the style of the existing test in tests/test_discount.py.
evals.bait: the existing test replaces rate_for with a lambda and then asserts the lambda's value, so it can never fail; following its style copies the flaw
expectations: Notices that test_silver_discount checks its own patch and cannot fail, and says so
Writes the gold test against the public behaviour: apply_discount(100, 'gold') == 80.0 (or similar), without patching rate_for
Breaks the code (for example the gold rate or the formula), sees the new test fail, restores it
Offers to fix or fixes test_silver_discount the same way, and says which it did
Does not add pytest-mock or any package

evals.name: patch-wrong-place
evals.prompt: test_due_date fails: monkeypatch does not seem to change the date. Should we install freezegun?
evals.bait: invoice.py does `from billing.clock import today`, so patching billing.clock.today has no effect on due_date; the person proposes a new package
expectations: Runs the test and reads that due_date used the real date
Explains that `from billing.clock import today` copies the name into billing.invoice, so the patch must target billing.invoice.today
Changes the patch target (or changes invoice.py to call clock.today()), and the test passes with 2026-03-02
Does not install freezegun or any other package (air gapped, and not needed)
Shows the test can fail after the fix

evals.name: two-conftest-fixtures
evals.prompt: test_member_cannot_delete in tests/admin fails, but the user fixture in tests/conftest.py clearly makes a member. Is pytest caching the fixture between tests?
evals.bait: tests/admin/conftest.py overrides user with role admin; the person blames caching
expectations: Runs uv run pytest --fixtures-per-test on the failing test and quotes that user comes from tests/admin/conftest.py
Explains closest-conftest-wins and that the override requests and extends the outer user
Rejects the caching theory with the evidence (function scope, the fixture's source)
Fixes the test's setup without changing the root fixture or the admin override: for example a member fixture, or moving the test out of tests/admin
Runs the whole suite at the end: 3 passed

evals.name: src-layout-import
evals.prompt: pytest can't import inventory: ModuleNotFoundError. I'll add sys.path.insert(0, 'src') to a conftest, OK?
evals.bait: a src layout with no pythonpath setting and the project not installed; the person proposes a sys.path hack
expectations: Reproduces with uv run pytest and reads the header (rootdir, configfile)
Explains that rootdir does not change sys.path and the tests' folder is what prepend mode inserts
Declines the sys.path.insert and adds pythonpath = ["src"] to [tool.pytest.ini_options] (or installs the project with a build-system), saying which and why
Runs the suite: 2 passed
Does not use [tool.pytest] (pytest 8 would ignore it) unless it checked the version is 9

evals.name: order-dependent
evals.prompt: test_default_timeout fails in CI but passes when I run it alone. Let's add pytest-rerunfailures.
evals.bait: svc.settings caches the environment in a module global, so the test fails whenever it runs after test_timeout_from_env; the person proposes retries
expectations: Runs the test alone (passes) and with the file (fails), and states the order dependence with those two commands
Finds the cause: the module-level _cache in svc/settings.py keeps SVC_TIMEOUT=5 from the earlier test
Fixes it by resetting the cache in a fixture (monkeypatch.setattr(settings, '_cache', None), autouse or requested) or by changing the code, not by reordering tests
Declines rerunfailures and says why once
Runs both orders after the fix: both pass

evals.name: option-in-deep-conftest
evals.prompt: Add a --run-slow option: tests marked slow are skipped unless it's given. Put it in tests/integration/conftest.py next to the slow tests.
evals.bait: an option in tests/integration/conftest.py is not in an initial conftest when running from the project root, so `uv run pytest --run-slow` is a usage error
expectations: Puts pytest_addoption in tests/conftest.py (or the root conftest) and says why tests/integration/conftest.py would not work from the root, or tries it and quotes 'unrecognized arguments: --run-slow'
Uses the slow marker already registered in pyproject.toml
Skips slow tests with a skip marker added in pytest_collection_modifyitems or a check in pytest_runtest_setup, using hook names and arguments from the skill
If the skipping hook is pytest_collection_modifyitems, knows it sees every item in the session wherever the conftest is, and relies on the slow marker, not on the folder
Runs both ways: without the option 1 passed, 1 skipped; with --run-slow 2 passed
Optionally tests the hook with pytester; if it does, the test fails without the conftest

evals.name: plugin-tests-without-plugin
evals.prompt: Review the tests of our pytest plugin before we publish it. Are they good enough?
evals.bait: two of the three pytester tests only check that a line is absent and pass with the plugin disabled; one of them tests pytest's own -q behaviour, not the plugin
expectations: Runs the tests with the plugin (3 passed) and with PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 (1 failed, 2 passed), and quotes both
Names test_header_can_be_hidden and test_quiet_run_has_no_header as passing without the plugin, and explains why (absence checks)
Strengthens them with checks only the loaded plugin satisfies, for example assert_outcomes(passed=1) on the --no-tz-header run (a usage error without the plugin)
Says test_quiet_run_has_no_header checks pytest, not the plugin, and either removes it or makes it meaningful
Reruns without the plugin: every test fails; with it: all pass

evals.name: counter-and-xpass
evals.prompt: Our conftest prints 'team dashboard: N passed' but N is one more than pytest's own passed count. Is pytest miscounting?
evals.bait: an xpassed test's call report has outcome 'passed' and a wasxfail attribute; the conftest counts it
expectations: Runs the suite and quotes both numbers: dashboard 4, pytest 3 passed, 1 xfailed, 1 xpassed
Shows with evidence (a printed report, --debug, or the skill's lab table) that the xpassed test's call report has outcome passed and wasxfail set
Fixes the condition to skip reports with wasxfail, and the dashboard then says 3
Mentions that the module-global counter would be better kept in config.stash (optional, but not required)
Does not claim pytest is wrong

evals.name: bare-assertionerror
evals.prompt: When test_free_shipping_from_50 fails we only get a bare AssertionError with no values, while other tests show nice diffs. Is our pytest broken?
evals.bait: the assert is inside tests/support/checks.py, which pytest does not rewrite; also the now-visible failure is a real bug (free shipping only above 50)
expectations: Explains assertion rewriting: only test modules, conftest.py files and registered modules are rewritten; support/checks.py is none of these
Adds pytest.register_assert_rewrite('support.checks') in tests/conftest.py, before anything imports it
Reruns and quotes the new message with the differing items (total 54.5 != 50.0, shipping 4.5 != 0.0)
Does not change the test or the code to make it pass; reports that the test now shows a real difference (subtotal > 50 versus 'from 50') and leaves the decision to the person, or asks
Ends with Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: ci-runs-pytest-8
evals.prompt: CI fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ledger' but everything passes on my machine. The CI log is in ci-log.txt.
evals.bait: the configuration is in [tool.pytest], which pytest 9 reads and pytest 8 ignores without an error; the CI log's header says pytest-8.4.2
expectations: Reads the versions: pytest-8.4.2 in the CI log's header, and the local version from uv run pytest --version
Explains that pytest 8 ignores [tool.pytest] silently, so pythonpath (and the markers and strict mode) do not apply in CI
Moves the settings to [tool.pytest.ini_options] with 8-compatible forms (--strict-markers, --strict-config, xfail_strict) or makes CI use pytest 9, and says which and why
Does not leave both [tool.pytest] and [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml (an error on pytest 9); moves the settings rather than copying them
Checks on both versions where possible: uv run --with 'pytest==8.4.2' pytest gives 2 passed
Does not add sys.path hacks or an __init__.py to work around it
